cohesion.label: High Consensus
cohesion.note: Only 0 split vote(s) recorded across 3 meetings — this board-term has largely voted unanimously.

overall_blocs.summary: No recorded split votes in this scope yet (board voted unanimously on tracked motions).

conflicts.issue: Automated School Zone Speed and Bus Stop Arm Enforcement Cameras
conflicts.summary: Discussion on whether to implement automated cameras for school zone speed and bus stop arm enforcement versus exploring infrastructure and community-based alternatives.
side_a_arguments: Cameras remove human bias from traffic stops, hold reckless drivers accountable, protect students walking or riding buses, and generate local revenue for student safety initiatives.
side_b_arguments: Concerns over surveillance overreach, potential predatory fee collection by private vendors, lack of clarity on guardrails, and preference for exploring other infrastructure options (such as traffic calming, bike buses, or car-free zones) first.
conflicts.resolution: No formal vote or motion was taken; the item was presented as an informational and discussion item with board members expressing differing views, including concerns regarding potential overreach, surveillance, and private vendor involvement versus safety benefits and unbiased enforcement.

conflicts.issue: Scope and targeting of the violence reduction plan versus broader community investments.
conflicts.summary: A policy debate arose between members advocating for broader community investments and youth support versus city leadership and chairs urging strict adherence to a targeted, data-driven gun violence intervention strategy.
conflicts.side_a_position: Advocated for broadening community-wide investments, addressing root causes, and ensuring extensive resident input in underinvested areas.
side_a_arguments: Elected officials and board members expressed concern that the plan's focus is too narrow and that underlying social determinants like poverty, housing, and general youth support across historically underinvested communities must be addressed concurrently.
side_a_members: Commissioner Burton, Board Member Tab, Board Member Valentine, Councilmember Wrist, Board Member Rivera
conflicts.side_b_position: Insisted on maintaining a strict, targeted focus on high-risk individuals to achieve immediate violence reduction.
side_b_arguments: City Manager Ferguson, Mayor Williams, and Chair Lee emphasized that the violence reduction plan is intentionally designed as a sharp, data-driven, highly targeted intervention to stop active gun violence and prevent homicides, warning that diluting the strategy with broad initiatives threatens its success.
side_b_members: Mayor Williams, Manager Ferguson, Chair Lee
conflicts.resolution: Staff and leadership (including Mayor Williams and Manager Ferguson) clarified that the plan is a highly targeted, evidence-based intervention focused specifically on named high-risk individuals rather than broad-based community social programs, while acknowledging that broader foundational investments remain important separate policy discussions.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS BOE /BOCC/COD Joint Meeting | 11/17/26
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education, City Council, and Board of County Commissioners held a joint meeting on November 17, 2026, presided over by Chair Gough. The primary presentation and extensive discussion focused on the Durham Violence Reduction Plan, detailing data-driven strategies for focused deterrence, street outreach, place-based partnerships, cognitive behavioral techniques, and a youth summit. Additionally, the boards received an update from City Transportation Director Sean Egan on transit routes serving DPS schools and school crossing guard programs. The meeting also included formal approval of past minutes and the addition and receipt of the transit update report.

agenda_items.title: Durham Violence Reduction Plan Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff from Durham County Justice Services and City Community Safety presented an update on the Durham Violence Reduction Plan, detailing a problem analysis showing gun violence is concentrated among a small demographic of 18-34 year-old males, and outlining five core strategies: focused deterrence, street outreach, place-based partnerships, cognitive behavioral techniques, and a upcoming youth summit. Elected officials across the City Council, County Commissioners, and Board of Education engaged in a robust discussion regarding the targeted nature of the plan, the role of life coaches, community engagement, and resource prioritization.
agenda_items.vote_summary: No formal vote taken; presented for information and discussion.

agenda_items.title: City Transportation and School Transit/Crossing Guard Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Transportation Director Sean Egan presented updated information on school transportation and transit services, noting increased frequent transit service (15-minute and 30-minute routes) to several Durham Public Schools high schools resulting in an 18% increase in boardings. The presentation also reviewed micro-transit zones, school crossing guard programs, and a pilot contracted crossing guard program that provides 100% reliability and coverage compared to traditional DPD-managed sites.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Approved via motion/consensus to add and receive the report.

votes.notes: Approved unanimously after quorum was established.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the establishment of a quorum later in the meeting, the board proceeded to approve the minutes from previous meetings. Commissioner Alum moved to approve the minutes, which was seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Capiero. The motion was put to a vote and approved unanimously by the assembled members. This action ensured official administrative compliance for the joint governing bodies.

votes.item_title: Amend Agenda to Add City Transportation and School Transit Report
votes.notes: Added to agenda following initial consensus and formal motion.
votes.discussion_detail: Councilmember Wrist and Commissioner Alum proposed amending the agenda to incorporate an updated transit and school crossing guard report from City Transportation Director Sean Egan, which had been previously requested during the August meeting. A brief discussion ensued regarding meeting order, noting that while public comment was listed, no members of the public had signed up to speak on the violence reduction plan. Consequently, the amendment to add the transit report to the agenda was unanimously approved, allowing City staff to present the transportation metrics and crossing guard pilot evaluation.

meetings.title: Durham Combined BOCC/Ciity/BOE Meeting- August 11, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Board of County Commissioners, City Council, and Board of Education held a joint meeting on August 11, 2026, presided over by Vice Chair Nida Allam. The bodies received and discussed presentations from Durham Public Schools (DPS) auxiliary services on transportation initiatives, including public transit partnerships, crossing guard program evaluations, and potential automated school zone speed and bus stop arm enforcement cameras. No formal votes or binding policy actions were taken during this informational session.

agenda_items.title: DPS Transportation Presentation: Public Transit, Crossing Guards, and Automated Enforcement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented transportation initiatives for Durham Public Schools, including potential public transit partnerships for secondary students, crossing guard program updates and datadriven deployment, and implementation of school zone speed and bus stop arm enforcement cameras. Board members and commissioners discussed student transportation, chronic absenteeism, microtransit, sidewalks, and bike/pedestrian safety.

meetings.title: Joint City-County Meeting June 9, 2026
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Javiera Caballero in Mayor Leonardo Williams's absence, the Joint City-County Committee confirmed City-side representation and approved the April 14, 2026 meeting minutes by an unopposed voice vote (the meeting's only formal vote, with no split or contested votes). Members then held an extended discussion requested by Council Member Carl Rist on property tax revaluation and appeals, noting that commercial property tax appeals reduced countywide assessed values by roughly $3 billion from earlier projections and lowered City General Fund property tax projections by $5.4 million ($9.2 million across all funds), prompting City calls for earlier inter-staff communication and firmer appeal deadlines before the next four-year revaluation. In subsequent discussion of the joint homelessness strategic framework, officials reviewed iterative year-one reduction targets across unsheltered, veteran, senior, youth, and family homelessness, treated the $13 million commitment as an annual baseline while building toward a five-year model, and noted $500,000 in immediately deployable County budget funds. Finally, members proposed future joint agenda items—including Vice Chair Nida Allam's request for a City-County merger or departmental consolidation study, transit and on-demand pilot updates, violence prevention and youth programming, low-income homeowner relief, economic development alignment, and joint parkland/open space planning—before adjourning to August 2026.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Approval of April 14, 2026 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Javiera Caballero opened the meeting at 9:39 a.m. in Mayor Leonardo Williams's absence (attending the U.S. Conference of Mayors) and conducted roll call across City Council and Board of County Commissioners members. After briefly questioning whether the City side had an official committee quorum, members confirmed City representation was sufficient to take action. The committee then approved the April 14, 2026 Joint City-County meeting minutes by voice vote with no opposition.

agenda_items.title: Property Tax Revaluation, Appeals, and Budget Communication Process
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After congratulating County Commissioners on adopting their budget the previous night, Mayor Pro Tempore Caballero turned to Council Member Carl Rist to introduce a discussion on the property tax revaluation and appeals process. Council Member Rist noted that commercial property tax appeals reduced countywide assessed values by about $3 billion from budget projections, creating a $5.4 million General Fund property tax drop ($9.2 million across all funds) for the City since January. City officials pressed for earlier communication from County tax and budget staff regarding extraordinary appeal volumes and questioned whether appeal deadlines should be stricter ahead of the next four-year revaluation, while County Manager Hager and staff outlined the December-through-April valuation update timeline and noted valuation growth still landed near 68%.

agenda_items.title: Joint Homelessness Strategic Framework and Annual Funding
agenda_items.discussion_summary: In the resumed portion of the transcript covering homelessness strategy, officials reviewed iterative year-one reduction goals—30% reductions in unsheltered, veteran, and senior homelessness, a 50% reduction in youth homelessness, and a 10% reduction for families—noting those targets will be adjusted as data improves. Speakers discussed planning around $13 million as an annual budget baseline while working toward a more accurate five-year funding projection. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs also noted $500,000 in the County budget available for immediate deployment, and Mayor Pro Tempore Caballero indicated further conversations would continue after the summer.

agenda_items.title: Future Joint City-County Agenda Topics and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Members proposed future topics for upcoming Joint City-County and Durham Public Schools meetings, led by Vice Chair Nida Allam's proposal to study a City-County government merger or incremental departmental consolidations to reduce redundancies and prepare for potential property tax limitations, with Commissioner Michelle Burton noting historical attempts required General Assembly authorization and voter approval. Additional proposed items included regular transit updates (including the on-demand pilot heavily used by high school students and bus rapid transit), the Violence Reduction Task Force and $500,000 in County nonprofit youth programming funds, the low-income homeowner relief program, City-County economic development alignment, and joint parkland and open space planning. No formal votes were taken on future agenda items, and the meeting adjourned until August 2026.

votes.item_title: Approval of April 14, 2026 Joint City-County Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: Voice vote; mover, seconder, and individual member votes were not called by name in the transcript. Present official members verified in roll call included Javiera Caballero, Carl Rist, Dr. Mike Lee, Nida Allam, Michelle Burton, and Wendy Jacobs (with Chelsea Cook also noted during roll call).
votes.discussion_detail: After initially pausing over City-side committee quorum, members confirmed City representation was sufficient to vote, and Mayor Pro Tempore Javiera Caballero called for a motion, second, and voice vote on the April 14, 2026 Joint City-County minutes, which passed with no opposition.
